arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Mon: he asked her out for Saturday after Shabbat (a walk, falafel at Avi's); she said yes, 'things change in January'. Tue: trivia, Dana the quizmaster, HERZL HEADS second. Wed: she's short with a supplier, Lior lets slip she took Monday off 'up north'. Next: first date Sat Nov 21; she almost tells him.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Mon: Hanukkah files to Gadi only; Ruti asked for Ishai's number. Tue: Gadi phoned with a coffee-shop logo 'by Friday'. Wed: the number moves from Thursday to 'Sunday, Ofer is on reserve duty'; Ishai agrees to sketch only. Next: Ruti calls Ishai directly (week 2).
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Mon-Tue: the duffel and the taped box 'S.', 'three plumbers from the Mandate', a cracked call on the stairs. Wed morning: too much energy, coaches him for Saturday, Shir's calls face down. Wed night (second couch night): her phone lights with 'S.: the keys are with the neighbour'; he sees the preview and puts the phone down. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: The notebook: 'I want to talk to Dana', 'I want a date (payment kind)', 'I want: one invoice'. Wed: he holds a little with Gadi (sketch only until the number). Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Tue: deleted voice message to Eli. Wed: Moti took her to the clinic, 'maybe bronchitis', she calls it 'a little cold'; Moti asks Ishai to feed the cats in the mornings; 'busy' is the building's word for Eli. Next (week 2): bronchitis, she stays home; Ishai feeds the cats daily.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Tue: no proverb, a lawyer's envelope in his apron, a call he lets ring. Next (week 2): no proverbs at all.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Mon: chapter twelve, 'she says yes'. Wed: chapter thirteen, 'the man buys a coat for a cold city he's never been to'; lets slip Dana took Monday off 'up north' and backpedals. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Tue: trivia, argued every answer with Dana, showing off for Noa. Wed Nov 18: the Pump House gallery night (Quiet Signals) with Ishai.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

beats.goal: Morning after Noa's first couch night. She is up first with too much energy, makes coffee too strong, and coaches Ishai for Saturday's date with Dana (what to wear, no more than three sorries). Her phone buzzes face down twice; she doesn't look. She says the plumbers 'found more pipes', so she'll sleep here again tonight, after his Pump House night with Tomer. Ishai does NOT learn about Shir.
beats.teaser: Noa coaches Ishai for Saturday, and ignores her phone again
beats.forceText: Noa makes too-strong coffee and coaches Ishai for Saturday; her phone buzzes face down and she leaves it.

forceLines.say: Three sorries, max. After that you're apologising to the falafel.

forceCommentary.say: She's planning his date like a wedding. Who's planning hers?
Phone face down. Second morning running. That's a habit now.

moments.text: Morning. Noa is already up, hair tied, the armchair blanket folded too neatly. She hands Ishai a mug of coffee strong enough to stand a spoon in.

lines.say: Morning! I made coffee. I found your coffee. You hide it badly.
It's not hidden. It's in the coffee jar.
Exactly. Amateur. Drink. We have work to do.
What work? It's quarter to eight.
Saturday. Dana. You. A walk and falafel. We plan it now.
It's a walk. You put one foot in front of the other.
Wrong. You put one foot, you say something, then the other foot.
This coffee is illegal, Noa.
It's motivational. What are you wearing?
Clothes. The usual clothes.

commentary.say: Noa's running his love life at quarter to eight. Somebody's avoiding her own.
That coffee could restart a bus.

moments.text: At the island. Noa's phone buzzes face down beside her mug, twice. She covers it with her hand without looking and keeps talking.

lines.say: Rule one: three sorries, maximum. Four and I hear about it.
How would you hear about it?
I hear everything. Rule two: ask her a question and wait.
Wait how long?
Longer than you want to. Silence isn't a fire.
Your phone's buzzing again.
It's Eilat. The hug-in-August hotel. They can hug themselves.
You're allowed to answer in my kitchen.
I'm allowed not to. Rule three: the blue shirt. Not the pyjama trousers.
That was one time. On a video call.

commentary.say: She covered that phone like it was a hand of cards.
Rule four, apparently: never turn the phone over.

moments.text: Noa pulls on her coat on the landing with her bag on her shoulder, keys jangling. Below, someone's radio plays on the stairs.

lines.say: The plumbers found more pipes. Can I stay tonight too?
Of course. The armchair already knows you.
You have the Pump House with Tomer, right? I'll come after.
Come with us. It's art. Very quiet art.
Quiet's not my thing this week. I'll bring the good tea.
Noa. Last night on the stairs. You're okay?
Amazing. Ask me Saturday night, after your date.
That's not an answer, it's a schedule.
Yes, and it's a good schedule. Go walk your dog.

commentary.say: 'Ask me Saturday.' She's pushing it off like a deadline.
He asked twice in two days. That's a record for him.

update.memory: Second night on Ishai's armchair 'for the plumbers'. Coached him for Saturday: three sorries max. He asked if I'm okay. I said ask Saturday.

beats.goal: Lunch at Cafe Nahat. Dana is behind the counter, short and distracted on the phone with a milk supplier; she still draws a basil leaf on his cup but says little. Then Lior at his usual table reads 'chapter thirteen' (the man buys a coat for a cold city he has never been to) and lets slip that Dana took Monday off, 'family up north', then backpedals ('or south, I don't know geography'). Ishai knows her family is in Holon and is puzzled. He does NOT learn about Haifa.
beats.teaser: Dana's distracted, and Lior says one word too many
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Dana is distracted; Lior lets slip that she took Monday off 'up north', then backpedals.

forceLines.say: She's off Monday. Family up north. Or south. I'm a novelist, not a map.
Her family's in Holon. Holon is not north.

forceCommentary.say: Lior just dropped a crumb the size of a croissant.
Holon. Not north. The man knows his Holon.

moments.text: Lunchtime at Cafe Nahat. Dana is behind the counter with her phone pinned to her shoulder, arguing quietly about milk. She draws a small basil leaf on his cup without looking up.

lines.say: No, the oat milk Friday. Friday. Okay. Okay. Bye.
Hi. Problems with the cows?
With the people who drive the cows. Your usual?
My usual. And a cheese toast, please.
Leaf's a bit crooked today. Don't read into it.
I'll read nothing. I'm an illiterate customer.
Good. Saturday's still on, by the way. I didn't forget.
I didn't think you forgot. I hoped you didn't. Same thing.
Go sit. Lior's been saving you a chair, it's weird.
Thanks. Sorry. Not sorry. Thanks.

commentary.say: Crooked leaf, 'don't read into it'. I'm reading into it.
One sorry, one not-sorry. Net zero. Noa would allow it.

moments.text: At Lior's table by the window. Lior turns his laptop half toward Ishai and reads a paragraph aloud, very pleased with himself.

lines.say: Chapter thirteen. 'He bought a coat for a cold city he had never been to.'
Why would he buy a coat for a city he's not going to?
Exactly! That's the whole chapter. Hope, with buttons.
It's nice. A bit sad. Is he going?
I don't know yet. He doesn't know yet. Nobody tells him anything.
Poor guy. Someone should tell him.
Someone should. Speaking of nobody: Dana's off Monday. Family up north.
Up north? Her family's in Holon.
North. South. I'm a novelist, not a map. Forget I said it.
Forget what? You read me a coat.

commentary.say: 'Nobody tells him anything.' Lior, darling, you are the nobody.
Holon is south of here. The man checked the map in his head.

moments.text: The cheese toast arrives. Ishai eats slowly, glancing at Dana at the counter, who is back on the phone, turned toward the wall.

lines.say: Lior, what does 'things change in January' mean, to you?
Prices. In January everything changes. Rent, milk, people.
People?
People make resolutions. Then they keep one by accident.
She said it on Monday. When she said yes.
Then hold on to the yes. Writers hold on to the yes.
You're being strange today. Stranger. Normal strange plus.
I'm on chapter thirteen. It's an unlucky chapter. Eat your toast.
I want to ask her. Not now. Saturday.
Saturday's good. Saturdays are good for chapters.

commentary.say: 'I want to ask her.' The notebook is working, people.
Lior changed the subject faster than Dana changes milk suppliers.

update.memory: Read Ishai chapter thirteen, the coat. Let slip Dana is off Monday 'up north'. He knows her family's in Holon. He'll ask her Saturday.

beats.goal: At home at his desk, Gadi phones about the coffee-shop logo from yesterday ('a medium thing, paid with the rest'). Ishai asks for Thursday's number; Gadi moves it to Sunday ('Ofer is on reserve duty'). Ishai, deflated, agrees to send only a pencil sketch until the number arrives. Gadi laughs it off, cheerful. Phone only: Gadi is never seen.
beats.teaser: Gadi's Thursday number starts sounding like Sunday
beats.forceText: Gadi moves Thursday's invoice number to Sunday; Ishai agrees to send only a sketch until then.

forceLines.say: Sunday is basically Thursday with a weekend in the middle!
Then a sketch on Thursday. Files when the number comes.

forceCommentary.say: Thursday became Sunday. Watch Sunday become January.
A sketch. Pencil only. That's Ishai's version of a strike.

moments.text: Ishai at his desk, laptop open on a blank coffee-shop logo file. Gadi's call comes in; Ishai puts him on speaker and leans back.

lines.say: Ishai! My favourite pixel! How's the coffee shop coming?
It's a blank file and a cup of coffee. Research.
Love it. Friday, yes? It's a medium thing, paid with the rest.
About the rest. Tomorrow's Thursday. The number?
The number. Yes. So. Ofer is on reserve duty till Sunday.
Ofer is always somewhere till Sunday.
Sunday is basically Thursday with a weekend in the middle!
That's not what basically means, Gadi.
It's what it means at Sababa. Everything's coming, together, beautifully.
Together. Yes. I've heard of together.

commentary.say: 'My favourite pixel.' He only says that when he's about to borrow something.
Ofer has been on reserve, migrating, and printing. Ofer is a very busy man.

moments.text: Ishai stands up and walks to the window, phone at his ear, looking at Moshe while he talks. The notebook lies open on the desk behind him.

lines.say: Okay. Here's what I can do. A pencil sketch, Thursday.
A sketch? The client wants colours, Ishai. Joy!
Joy comes with the files. Files come when the number comes.
Who taught you that? Was it Noa? It sounds like Noa.
It was a notebook. Long story.
Fine. Fine! A sketch. Sunday the number, Sunday the joy.
Sunday. In writing, please.
I'll text you a thumbs up. That's writing now.
It's a thumb. Thanks, Gadi.
You're the best. Small change, big heart. Bye!

commentary.say: He held the line! A pencil line, but a line.
A thumbs up as a contract. Moshe has more legal standing.

update.memory: Coffee-shop logo by Friday. Moved the number to Sunday, Ofer on reserve. Ishai will only send a pencil sketch until the number comes.

beats.goal: On the landing Moti is coming up with a pharmacy bag: he drove Mrs. Levi to the clinic, 'maybe bronchitis', she calls it 'a little cold' and is resting behind her door. Moti asks Ishai to feed her cats in the mornings this week. Ishai asks about Eli; Moti says 'busy' is the building's word for Eli and that it is not his place, not yet. Mrs. Levi is not seen (she only coughs behind her door). Ishai does NOT learn her secret.
beats.teaser: Moti comes up the stairs with Mrs. Levi's pharmacy bag
beats.forceText: Moti brings Mrs. Levi's medicine up from the clinic, 'maybe bronchitis', and asks Ishai to feed her cats this week.

forceLines.say: Bronchitis, maybe. She says a little cold. She also says Eli is busy.
I'll do the cats. Mornings. Every morning.

forceCommentary.say: 'She also says Eli is busy.' Moti, say the rest.
The committee book holds the receipts and, apparently, the secrets.

moments.text: Moti climbs the last stairs with a white pharmacy bag and a box of tissues, breathing hard. From behind Mrs. Levi's door, a long cough.

lines.say: Ishai. Good. Hold this, my knees are on strike.
What's all this? Is it for Mrs. Levi?
I drove her to the clinic. Two hours in the waiting room.
And? What did they say?
Bronchitis, maybe. An X-ray Sunday. She says 'a little cold'.
That cough is not a little cold.
Tell her. She'll give you a lecture on cold. I got one in the car.
Should I knock?
She's sleeping. Or pretending. Leave the bag by the door.

commentary.say: Two hours in a waiting room with Mrs. Levi. Moti deserves a medal.
An X-ray Sunday. Everything in this building happens Sunday.

moments.text: Ishai sets the bag down by Mrs. Levi's door. Ben-Gurion the grey cat sits on the stairs, staring at both of them.

lines.say: The cats. She's worried about the cats more than her lungs.
I'll do the cats. Mornings. Every morning this week.
Good. The grey one only eats if you talk to him.
Ben-Gurion. I know. What do I say to him?
Anything. Politics. He's a good listener, bad voter.
Moti, should someone call Eli? Her son?
Eli is busy. That's the word in this building. Busy.
You said it like it's in quotes.
It's not my place, Ishai. Not yet. Feed the cats.
Okay. Not yet. But yet comes, right?

commentary.say: 'Not yet.' Moti knows something and it's eating him.
Ben-Gurion is a good listener, bad voter. Finally, a fair description of a cat.

update.memory: Drove Mrs. Levi to the clinic, maybe bronchitis. Ishai will feed her cats every morning. He asked about Eli. I said not yet.

beats.goal: After the Pump House gallery night, Noa arrives for her second couch night with 'the good tea'. She asks about the art and about Tomer ('did he talk through all of it?'), laughs too loud, then falls asleep in the armchair mid-sentence. Ishai covers her with a blanket; her phone lights up on the armrest with a preview 'S.: The keys are with the neighbour. Take care of yourself.' He reads only that, says out loud it isn't his phone, and turns it face down. Ishai does NOT learn about Shir.
beats.teaser: Noa's second night on the armchair, and her phone lights up
beats.forceText: Noa falls asleep in the armchair; her phone lights up with a message from 'S.' about keys, and Ishai turns it face down.

forceLines.say: 'S. The keys are with the neighbour.' ...Not your phone, Ishai.

forceCommentary.say: 'S.' Again. The box says S. The phone says S. Ishai, my love.
He turned it face down. Integrity, or fear of tape. Same face.

moments.text: Noa comes in with a tin of tea and her pillow, cheeks pink from the cold. Ishai is still in his jacket from the Pump House.

lines.say: The good tea, as promised. So? Was the art quiet?
Very quiet. Tomer wasn't.
Ha! Did he talk through all of it?
He told Hagit a painting looked like an electrical fault.
Was it?
A bit. 'Still Water'. It had a wire in it. Metaphorically.
Did Tomer ask about me?
Twice. Why?
No reason. Tomer asks about everybody. Kettle!
Kettle. Yes.

commentary.say: 'Did Tomer ask about me?' Oh, she noticed. Tomer, she noticed.
An electrical fault is the highest compliment an electrician can give.

moments.text: Tea in two mugs. Noa curls into the armchair under the blanket, talking faster and faster, then slower. Falafel lies at her feet.

lines.say: Saturday. Remember rule two. Ask, then wait. Silence isn't a fire.
Silence isn't a fire. I wrote it down.
You wrote it in the notebook? In my notebook?
Your notebook. My want list. Page three.
What's on page three?
Ask Noa what's wrong. And wait.
...That's a terrible thing to write in a gift.
I'm waiting. Silence isn't a fire.
Tomorrow. I'm so tired, Ishush. Five minutes. Then I tell you about the...
About the what? Noa?

commentary.say: He used her own rule on her. And she folded. Into sleep.
'Ask Noa what's wrong.' Page three. Somebody hand this man a medal.

moments.text: Noa is asleep in the armchair, mouth open. Ishai pulls the blanket up to her shoulders. Her phone on the armrest lights up; he reads the preview without touching it, then turns it face down.

lines.say: Asleep. Mid-sentence. Classic.
'S. The keys are with the neighbour. Take care of yourself.'
Not your phone, Ishai. Not your phone.
Goodnight, Noa. Whatever it is.

commentary.say: 'S.' The box says S. The phone says S. Ishai, my love, connect it.
He turned it face down. He's learning her habits.

update.memory: Second night at Ishai's. Fell asleep in his armchair before I could tell him. He wrote 'ask Noa what's wrong' in my notebook.

hook.text: Noa fell asleep before she could say it, and her phone read 'S.: the keys are with the neighbour'. Whose keys, and who is S.?

previously.text: On the stairs Noa ended a call: 'not on the phone, not tonight', and said everything is amazing. Ishai went to bed with the 'S.' box still taped.

hosts: Wednesday. Lecture at eleven, the Pump House at eight. Quiet art tonight. Tomer has never been quiet.
Noa slept on the armchair. Night one. Ask me how many nights the plumbers need.
Three plumbers from the British Mandate. I want to meet them. I have questions about lead.
Moshe the basil is leaning toward the window. Oren says that's growth. I say that's escape.
It's called phototropism, Zohar. He's reaching for the light. Like all of us.
Gadi promised a number by Thursday. Tomorrow is Thursday. Place your bets.
Quiet Signals at the Pump House: art by Roni Lavi. Hagit says no talking. Tomer has read that as a challenge.
Saturday, after Shabbat: a walk and falafel. Three days. Somebody tell Ishai to breathe.
Last night HERZL HEADS came second. Eighteen out of thirty. The sports round saved them, and Tomer will never let it go.
That box marked 'S.' has now lived by the closet longer than some of my relationships.
Mrs. Levi's cough has a cough now.
Lior has been writing chapter thirteen for a week. Some chapters are long. Some are suspicious.
Avi's queue at half past six. Best falafel on Herzl. Proverbs not included this week, apparently.
Mrs. Levi's game show at half past seven. She'll be watching from bed, probably shouting in a whisper.
Nobody on this street says what they mean this week. It's like a soap opera with tahini.
Sixteen degrees and partly cloudy. Jacket weather, for Tel Aviv. Parka weather, for Ishai.
If Ishai says sorry fewer than ten times today, Oren buys the coffee.
I'm not buying anything. I've seen this man apologise to a door.
Falafel the dog has been to a lecture, a quiz and a gallery this week. More culture than me.
Today's lecture, Strange But True. Eleven o'clock. Ishai takes notes like there's a test. There's no test.
Ben-Gurion the cat only eats if you talk to him. Relatable.
Thursday tomorrow: improv lesson three. 'Yes, and.' Our man is getting dangerous.
Somebody in this building keeps saying 'Sunday'. Everything's Sunday. Sunday is the new later.
Dana drew a crooked leaf yesterday. Or was it the day before. I keep a spreadsheet, don't judge me.
Gallery tonight, film on Saturday: The Island of Doctor Moreau. Ishai's calendar is more fun than mine.
Quiet morning so far. Which in this show means something loud is on the way.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, good morning to the early birds and the people who are only pretending.
Sixteen degrees, partly cloudy. Bring a jacket, leave the excuses.
Traffic on Herzl is moving. Slowly. Like my uncle at a wedding buffet.
This one goes out to everyone waiting for a payment. Hang in there. It's 'in the system'.
Fun fact: Wednesday is the only day that sounds like a sneeze if you say it fast enough.
Tonight at the Pump House, art you have to look at in silence. Practise at home with your in-laws.
Shuk Shalom says the clementines are in. I say the clementines were always in. They're clementines.
Callers asking about the weekend: it's coming. Friday at least. Saturday, probably.
Somebody texted the station: 'my neighbour coughs through the wall, is that a song?' Get well soon, neighbour.
Next up, a song about rain. We have no rain. We have the song.
Radio Herzl, the station that's been on longer than your landlord's promises.
Late night now. If you're still up, drink water, call your mother, turn your phone face up.

zelig: The pigeons were here before the bank. The bank thinks otherwise.
A man who waits needs a good bench and a bad memory.
Not this sea. A colder one. Someone is always going to a colder one.
In 1971 I almost left. I stayed. Ask me if I'm sorry. Don't.
michal: Friday run club, seven sharp. I'll be there in spirit.
Mirror says good. Mirror lies. Mirror is my friend.
He walks on the treadmill like he's apologising to it.
sivan: Ten an hour. Eleven on Wednesdays.
Plumbers at seven. Sure. And I'm a marathon princess.
The husky guy didn't come today. Good. Less traffic.
lior: He bought a coat for a city he'd never seen. No. He looked at a coat.
Don't say north. Why did I say north.
Some characters don't know they're characters. That's the best kind.
She's on the phone again. With the wall.
kobi: Wednesday's numbers: four, eleven, and the age I feel.
The lottery is a tax on hope. I pay my taxes.
One more and then I'm going home. That was three ones ago.
Everybody's in love in this town except the barman. And me. And the barman.

street: ...he said Sunday, and I said which Sunday...
...the 88 came twice and then never again...
...I'm not cold, I'm Israeli, it's different...
...my cousin moved up north, she says it's quiet, too quiet...
market: ...clementines, three kilos for ten, who eats three kilos...
...no, the other dill, the one that smells like dill...
park: ...the duck has a name, I'm not telling you...
...two laps and then coffee, that's the deal...
...he talks to the pigeons, they answer, I don't ask...
cafe: ...oat milk Friday, she said Friday three times...
...I'm writing too, but in my head, it's faster...
...a new place in January, everything's new in January...

chat.say: Reminder: the stair light on 2 is fixed. Please do not hang anything on it. Moti
Whose is the blue bicycle in the entrance? It is very beautiful and very in the way.
Mrs. Levi is resting today. Please knock softly, or better, don't knock. Moti
Who wants clementines? I bought three kilos, I don't know why.
Bicycle still there. Still beautiful. Still in the way.
Medicine for Apt 3 is by her door. Please do not move the bag.
I am fine. A little cold. Who has the remote for Channel 9, mine is lost
Clementines left by the mailboxes. Take. Please. I beg.
